channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
item.description: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend for Codex-scale development across its monorepo, cutting median push latency nearly 5x while transferring close to 1PB of Git data daily. (OpenAI News)

item.title: The latest AI news we announced in October 2026
item.description: Gemini 4 Argon launched globally for developers and enterprises in October 2026, followed two weeks later by Gemini 4 Carbon for long-term engineering and cybersecurity defense, with Google also introducing Genie 4 for real-time interactive simulations. (Google AI Blog)

item.title: Security risk assessments include repository protection status
item.description: Security risk assessments include repository protection status (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
item.description: OpenAI's Grid Protectors Program pairs future compute campuses with utilities to cut power use when the grid is strained, including a Georgia Power agreement for up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response, aiming to protect consumer electricity costs. (OpenAI News)

item.title: pull_request_target blocked by default December 2
item.description: GitHub Actions will block pull_request_target events by default in all public repositories from December 2, 2026, unless an Actions event policy explicitly allows them, after a delay from November 2, with Insights available until November 9 to identify affected workflows. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: LifeVal
item.description: LifeVal, OpenAI's new benchmark, tests whether AI can help with everyday tasks like finding childcare, managing finances and government paperwork, drawing on a 3,995-person survey and two time-use studies for over 1 billion weekly ChatGPT users. (OpenAI News)

item.title: ChatGPT to proactively end dangerous conversations, ban repeat offenders outright
item.description: OpenAI will add stricter violence safeguards to ChatGPT in the coming weeks, letting the model end conversations that persistently focus on violence or serious harm and banning accounts repeatedly cut off. (AIbase)

item.title: Hexi 2077 AI Deep Signal Weekly, 2026 W44: The Verification Deficit and Compute Rent
item.description: With 88,000 of 1.53 million Agent skills carrying release clauses and scanners detecting at most 46%, this weekly report maps AI's verification deficit and asks who holds judgment over Anthropic's $120.5 billion compute spend. (Daily Digest)

item.title: Qodo builds context into AI code review with Codex
item.description: Qodo's Codex plugin injects company rules and cross-repository context into coding sessions, running independent reviews that catch P0 issues before a pull request in customer environments exceeding 10,000 repositories. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Six steps to joint audio-video generation! Pika open-sources Pika H3 Flex, built on MiniMax H3
item.description: Pika H3 Flex, built on MiniMax H3, open-sources adapter weights and full inference code and jointly generates audio and video in just six denoising steps, reaching eighth on DesignArena’s text-to-video leaderboard as its highest-ranked open-source video model. (AIbase)

item.title: Beijing introduces smart glasses consumer policy: 15% subsidy on new purchases, up to 500 yuan per item
item.description: Beijing's Commerce Bureau issued a seven-measure smart glasses consumption guide offering a 15% purchase subsidy capped at 500 yuan per item, alongside support for first-store launches and departure tax refunds. (AIbase)

item.title: Cracking the AI long-term memory bottleneck, Alibaba Cloud powers Personal Agents toward deep personalization
item.description: Alibaba Cloud’s November 2 Memory service upgrade targets Personal Agent long-term memory and personalization, scoring 56.82 on PersonaMem-v2 to lead eight systems and ranking first on seven of nine tasks. (AIbase)

item.title: Ant Afu wins the World Internet Conference Leading Science and Technology Award, becoming the first health AI app to receive the honor
item.description: Ant Group's health AI Ant Afu won the Leading Science and Technology Award at the 2026 World Internet Conference, becoming the first vertical health AI app to receive it, with 150 million users and nearly 20 million daily health consultations. (AIbase)

item.title: Apple’s ‘Ultra’ smart home robot might have to wait until 2028
item.description: Apple's rumored J595 desktop robot, possibly named HomeView Ultra, has had hardware finished for about two years while software lags, pushing its launch to 2028 with a 9-inch swiveling screen, FaceTime tracking and a possible price above $1,000. (The Verge)

item.title: Cedric AI for Meetings — The first AI agent to present your slides and attend for you
item.description: Cedric AI for Meetings is billed as the first AI agent that presents your slides and attends meetings on your behalf, though a CAPTCHA gate left the page's claimed details unverified. (Product Hunt)

item.title: South Korea's largest-ever budget: 820 trillion won, with AI and semiconductors front and center
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung unveiled a record 820.9 trillion won 2027 budget on November 2, with 21.3 trillion won allocated to semiconductors, physical AI and AI data centers. (AIbase)

item.title: Baidu Search AI API costs just 4.9 yuan per 1,000 calls, undercutting DeepSeek
item.description: Baidu's upgraded Search AI API costs 4.9 yuan per 1,000 calls during its promotion—below DeepSeek's search API—and its four-layer AI-native architecture lifts content credibility over 50%, with API, MCP and Skill access aimed at Agent developers. (InfoQ CN)

item.title: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
item.description: The New York Times and other publications have sued Brave Software, alleging the browser scrapes their content to train AI, lets users bypass paywalls, and supplies stolen copyrighted material to AI firms including Anthropic and Perplexity. (The Verge)

item.title: Oracle Files to Issue $20 Billion in New Shares and Bonds to Fund AI Buildout
item.description: Oracle filed plans on Monday to raise $20 billion by issuing new shares and more debt, funding its artificial intelligence buildout. (www.cnbc.com)

item.title: Linkly AI Clipper — Save web as an Agent-friendly Markdown browser extension
item.description: Linkly AI Clipper is a browser extension that saves web pages as Agent-friendly Markdown, aiming to make web content easier for AI agents to read and use. (Product Hunt)
